description:
`docs/operations/repo-admin-settings.md:16-25` documents that
`can_approve_pull_request_reviews: true` is set at the repo level (alongside
`default_workflow_permissions: read`). The stated reason is that the
`develop-post-merge.yml` `auto-revert-on-failure` job needs it so a
`GITHUB_TOKEN`-driven `gh pr edit --add-reviewer` call can request review on
the auto-revert PR from the original PR author when the GraphQL author lookup
succeeds (confirmed: `develop-post-merge.yml` uses `--add-reviewer`, not an
approval call — the setting is currently unused for approvals, only enabling
the *capability*).

NOTE (2026-07-18): the review requirement this item's premise waits on was
RETIRED without being applied (see docs/operations/repo-admin-settings.md,
"Soundness-path review enforcement (RETIRED 2026-07-18)", and the closed
_project/DONE/main/planning/auto-merge-review-gate-admin-enforcement.yaml).
This item therefore stays dormant UNLESS a retirement revisit trigger fires
— in particular, agent PRs moving to a separate bot identity, at which
point require_code_owner_review becomes enforceable and this loophole
analysis becomes live again. Re-read it then; do not act on it before.

Original premise: once the review requirement from
auto-merge-review-gate-admin-enforcement is
actually enforced at the ruleset layer (required_approving_review_count>=1,
require_code_owner_review=true), this dormant capability becomes a live
self-approval loophole: any workflow running with a `pull-requests: write`
`GITHUB_TOKEN` could, in principle, call the PR-review-approve API and satisfy
the review requirement without a human ever looking at the diff — including
for a soundness-path PR. Today the setting only enables *requesting* review,
not approving one, and no workflow in this repo currently calls the approve
endpoint — but the capability being switched on repo-wide means a future
workflow change (or a compromised/malicious workflow run) could exploit it
silently, with no code-level signal that it happened.

anti_patterns.dont: flip can_approve_pull_request_reviews off without first confirming (w1/w2) what actually depends on it
anti_patterns.why: the auto-revert flow already exists and regressing its reviewer-request behavior would be a new incident, not a fix.

anti_patterns.dont: treat this as blocking auto-merge-review-gate-admin-enforcement's admin action
anti_patterns.why: this item is a followup once that enforcement is live, not a precondition for it.

preserves.behavior: The develop-post-merge.yml auto-revert-on-failure job's reviewer-request behavior (requesting review from the original PR author) continues to work if the setting is flipped off — verify with a dry run or by re-reading the GraphQL/--add-reviewer code path before applying the PUT.
docs/operations/repo-admin-settings.md remains the single source of truth for this setting's current value — do not let the runbook and live repo config drift.

prior_art.concept: .github/workflows/develop-post-merge.yml (~lines 106, 244, 374, 420) — the auto-revert-on-failure job's GraphQL author lookup and `gh pr edit ... --add-reviewer` call; confirm this is the only consumer of the capability before deciding to flip it off.

docs/operations/repo-admin-settings.md:16-25 — the setting and its stated justification (auto-revert reviewer-request flow); this item re-evaluates whether that justification still requires the capability once review enforcement is live.

verifications.description: No workflow currently submits an approving review via GITHUB_TOKEN
verifications.expected: no matches (or only the documented --add-reviewer reviewer-request call, which is a different API surface)

verifications.description: If flipped off, verify the live setting matches the runbook
verifications.expected: can_approve_pull_request_reviews matches whatever value docs/operations/repo-admin-settings.md now documents

work_units.notes:
Grep .github/workflows/ for pull_request_review_write-equivalent gh api
calls (e.g. `gh api ... /pulls/.../reviews` with an APPROVE event, or
`gh pr review --approve`) to establish the current blast radius is zero.
Record the grep command and result in the PR body — this is the w0-style
evidence re-check this item's description leans on.
work_units.summary: Confirm no workflow calls the PR-approve API today (only reviewer-request)

work_units.notes:
The GraphQL lookup + --add-reviewer call requests review, which per GitHub's
API does not itself require can_approve_pull_request_reviews (that setting
only gates the Actions token's ability to submit an approving/requesting
*review event* via the reviews API, not the lighter-weight reviewer
assignment via `gh pr edit --add-reviewer`, which uses the requested
reviewers list, not a review submission). Verify this distinction against
current GitHub Actions token permission docs before concluding the setting
is unnecessary — do not assume from the doc text alone.
work_units.summary: Re-evaluate whether the auto-revert flow actually needs can_approve_pull_request_reviews

work_units.notes:
If w2 confirms the auto-revert flow does not need
can_approve_pull_request_reviews, apply
`gh api -X PUT repos/joeharris76/BenchBox/actions/permissions/workflow
-f default_workflow_permissions=read -F can_approve_pull_request_reviews=false`
(admin action — cannot be done by an agent PR, same class of deferred
action as the ruleset PUT in auto-merge-review-gate-admin-enforcement) and
update docs/operations/repo-admin-settings.md to reflect the new value and
history entry. If the flow genuinely needs it (or flipping it off is
infeasible for another reason), instead add an explicit "Accepted residual
risk" subsection to the runbook naming the self-approval loophole,
why it's accepted, and what would need to change to close it.
work_units.summary: Flip the setting off if unneeded, or document the accepted residual risk
